speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me; I understand you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To help me narrow down the cause, how long has this been going on, and has the redness spread to your knuckles or palm?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mechanism of injury—being caught and pulled forcefully while playing football—is highly suggestive of a flexor tendon avulsion (often called a "Jersey Finger"). Given the acute onset and specific trauma, have you noticed any deformity of the fingertip or an inability to actively flex the tip of that finger compared to the others? Also, is the pain located at the tip of the finger or more proximally near the palm?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of right hand.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus). The history of forceful extension of a flexed finger during contact sports, combined with acute pain and swelling of the ring finger, is pathognomonic for this injury. Immediate surgical consultation is required for potential tendon repair.
